level: Agent-side persistent workspace roots-generation binding and fail-closed invalidation
componentAcceptance: verified on three platforms: same-config restarts keep admissions meaningful; a changed roots configuration fences unsettled admissions; ping exposes the digest
productAcceptance: partial; managed workspace ownership/permissions, cross-Agent dataDir coordination, external-writer CAS and the pinned-write Agent wiring remain open
implementation: rootsGeneration() digests the sorted [rootId, resolve(path)] pairs of the configured roots map; the digest is order-stable and never touches the filesystem

The digest persists in Store meta under workspaceRootsGeneration. A first run only records it; an observed change fences every surviving admission whose operation is unsettled (the legacy-fence liveness predicate), updates the meta row and writes a WORKSPACE_ROOTS_GENERATION_CHANGED audit row

withWorkspace fails new mutating operations with WORKSPACE_RECOVERY_REQUIRED while any generation-fenced operation is unsettled; plain reads never take the fence; settling the fenced operation (terminal with stop evidence) makes the fence inert without rollback
workspace_admissions gains a roots_generation column (ALTER, '' for pre-existing rows) recorded on every new admission for audit; replay still relies on the physical identity conflict check
machine_ping gains rootsGeneration as the documented preview-invalidation hook; the current Host ignores unknown ping fields, so no Host behavior changes

platforms.scope: existing verified fixture refresh-ui-20261030a; same five files uploaded via SFTP, SHA-256 spot-verified before the run

observed: A same-roots restart fences nothing: the surviving unknown admission still answers WORKSPACE_BUSY on its own physical root while other roots accept writes.

A changed roots configuration (root added, re-pointed or removed) fences every unsettled admission fail-closed: new mutating operations on any root answer WORKSPACE_RECOVERY_REQUIRED until the fenced operation settles, while plain reads continue and the audit row records the change.
Admin-settling the fenced operation makes the fence inert and the existing terminal trigger releases the admission; nothing is rolled back automatically.
machine_ping exposes the 64-hex digest; it is stable across key insertion order and changes whenever the roots mapping changes.
The suite is registered in npm test and therefore Windows/Ubuntu CI; existing workspace and write-path suites stay green on all three platforms.
limitations: The fence is Agent-instance scoped (one dataDir). Coordination across different Agent dataDirs on the same host, cross-machine root identity and external-writer CAS remain open.
Real 0600 ownership under container UID65532 and managed workspace ownership/permissions are not addressed; user projects are never chmod/chown-ed.
The current Host machine health projection does not yet surface rootsGeneration; the ping field is the hook for a future Host preview change, verified inert against the current Host contract tests.
A roots config change and back between two runs is observed as two changes; the second fence insert is idempotent for already-fenced operations.
pinned-write Agent wiring, permissions/config generation on the Host side, full command/CLI write facade, migration and live acceptance remain open.
